pages.observed: Frames 0 to 24. Empty small restaurant with open glass door at left, window landscape behind, host stand with desk phone and hanging bag at right. Caption appears at 0.6 s naming the only server at Wok and Karahi in Spring walking out. At 0.8 s the door panel has swung toward closing. No server figure is drawn.

Frames 30 to 54. Door closed at left, same medium room composition held for all five samples. Dark bag or apron hangs from the host stand side hook, slight sway. Caption about the only server walking out persists over the lower floor. No figure appears.

Frames 60 to 84. Medium room held to 2.4 s while a small Texas outline card draws in top right. Cut at 2.6 s to a close view of the host stand top: ruled pad, black desk phone and a dark apron hanging from a brass hook. At 2.8 s ring arcs appear on both sides of the handset. Caption remains; it overlaps the apron hook area.

Frames 90 to 114. Same close host stand shot held. The desk phone rings in pulses with arcs either side and a blinking amber lamp; no one answers. The Texas outline card finishes drawing. The caption band sits across the stand body and the apron hook.

Frames 120 to 144. Close host stand shot continues: phone keeps ringing in pulses with arcs, handset jiggles in the cradle, nobody answers. Locator card complete. The first caption clears after 4.4 s, leaving the apron visible below. No hand or figure.

Frames 150 to 174. Wide restaurant view: two guests seated at small tables under pendants before a large window, empty plates, a host stand cropped at the right with its pad and phone. The orange-shirt guest holds a menu and begins raising a hand. Figures are small, roughly a tenth of frame height. Caption asks who was going to take the order.
Frames 180 to 204. Wide shot held; the orange-shirt guest keeps a hand raised toward the stand while the phone at the cropped stand rings. Nothing else changes; no server arrives. Caption unchanged.

Frames 210 to 234. Wide room holds with the raised hand and ringing phone, caption clears at 7.4 s. At 7.8 s cut to the storefront: an empty blank sign frame hangs on the glass from a cup, a dark unlit flat panel stands on a pole beside the host stand where the apron hangs.

Frames 240 to 264. Medium storefront shot. The empty sign frame swings on its suction cup and settles, nothing pinned in it. The flat panel beside it remains dark. Caption reads The family didn't post a job ad. Frame occupies about a sixth of the screen height.
Frames 270 to 294. The storefront medium shot is held unchanged: blank sign frame upright, panel dark, host stand at right. No sampled motion during this second. Caption unchanged.

Frames 300 to 324. Same storefront composition with no sampled change; the panel is still dark and the sign frame still. Caption clears at 10.6 s. Combined with the prior page, the picture is unchanged for about two seconds.

Frames 330 to 354. Close shot of the flat host panel on its pole. Screen dark at 11.0 to 11.2 s, then a teal light wipes left to right, rings glow and the name Haniya writes across, complete at 11.8 s. Panel fills roughly the upper middle third, caption sits over the pole.
Frames 360 to 384. The lit panel reading Haniya is held in the same close framing. Rings pulse faintly; nothing else changes. No AI host tag yet.

Frames 390 to 414. Panel held, then at 13.4 s a tighter detail of the lit panel. A slate tag reading AI host is carried in from the upper right on its string toward the panel's corner eyelet; at 13.8 s it is near but not yet hooked. The caption crosses the lower panel screen.

Frames 420 to 444. The AI host tag reaches the panel's corner eyelet and hangs there over the top right of the lit screen, swinging slightly and settling. Haniya remains centered. Caption still across the lower screen.

Frames 450 to 474. Panel with tag held until 15.4 s. Cut at 15.6 s to a table top: a printed code card stands on the table with a plate and glass; a hand-held phone enters at the bottom, its screen already showing the camera view of the code. Phone and hand occupy the lower fifth of frame.

Frames 480 to 504. A hand with a blue sleeve lifts the phone up from the bottom; the phone's screen shows the code. It passes through the caption band at 16.4 s, then at 16.6 to 16.8 s it is raised in front of the real code card, occluding it, with the screen showing the code. Long bare forearm visible.

Frames 510 to 534. The phone is held up over the table on a very long forearm reaching from the bottom edge; the code card itself is hidden behind the phone. On screen the brackets have closed on the code (locked). At 17.8 s the menu sheet starts rising from the screen's bottom. The phone is roughly a fifth of frame height.

Frames 540 to 564. On the raised phone the menu slides up and covers the camera view, ending with a list of dish rows and Talk/Pay buttons. At phone scale the row text is too small to read in the sample; Chow mein is a tiny label. Arm and phone unchanged in position.

Frames 570 to 594. Cut at 19.2 s to a large close view of the phone's menu held in one hand. A second hand's index finger comes in from the right and presses the Chow mein row, which lights yellow at 19.8 s. The finger covers part of the label at contact. Readable: Chow mein, Talk, Pay.

Frames 600 to 624. The finger lifts off the lit Chow mein row and exits right by 20.4 s; the row stays lit yellow while the phone is held steady. No Talk use is shown. Pay button visible but not yet pressed.

Frames 630 to 654. The lit-row close holds with no caption to 21.2 s, then a cut to a smaller framing of the same phone. A second index finger rises from the lower right toward Pay by 21.8 s. Caption now reads and pays from a phone.

Frames 660 to 684. The finger presses Pay; the button becomes a red check mark and a large white card with a red check and the word Paid pops up over the menu. The finger withdraws and the Paid card is held. Phone occupies about a quarter of frame height.

Frames 690 to 714. The Paid confirmation holds on the phone, then at 23.6 s a cut to a kitchen pass: a black thermal printer on a steel cabinet under an empty leaning rail and a heat lamp, an empty dark wok on a cold burner to the right. No caption at 23.6 to 23.8 s.

Frames 720 to 744. The idle pass holds while the caption reads Nothing is cooked until the order is paid for. Cut at 24.6 s to a close two-shot of the paid phone at left and the printer at right; at 24.8 s a dashed red line arcs from the phone toward the printer top and a red paid mark lifts off the screen. Printer lamp still amber.

Frames 750 to 774. The red paid mark travels along a dashed arc from the phone over the rail into the printer's top slot by 25.4 s; at 25.6 s the printer lamp has turned red. At 25.8 s a tighter view of the printer with its red lamp, slot still empty; the caption band crosses the printer's lower front.

Frames 780 to 804. A ticket reading Chow mein with a red check rises out of the printer slot, reaches the rail and hangs, cut free with a torn edge, by 26.4 s. Cut to a wide pass: the ticket hangs above the printer, a cook's sleeved arm brings a steel bowl from the right and pours noodles into the wok as orange flame flares at 26.8 s. Only the cook's arm is visible.

Frames 810 to 834. The bowl finishes pouring and leaves; the wok, now full of noodles, sits in tall orange flame while the cook's hand rocks the handle at the right edge. The ticket hangs on the rail above the printer the whole time. Cook appears only as a sleeved forearm and hand at the frame edge.

Frames 840 to 864. Cut to a back office desk seen from the front: a cork board with an empty clip, a mug, and a ledger card sliding in from the right side, header Saving or winning back. The lower half of frame is plain dark desk front. Card is small, about a fifth of frame width at 28.8 s.

Frames 870 to 894. The ledger card finishes sliding and settles on the desk; its rows are empty and its header reads Saving or winning back in small type. The dollar figure appears only in the caption so far. Lower half of the frame is a plain dark desk front.

Frames 900 to 924. Closer on the ledger card; a kraft tag reading $9,650 a month drops from upper right and lands flat on the card's corner at 30.8 s, partly covering the header word back. Caption repeats the figure.
Frames 930 to 954. The $9,650 a month tag settles flat on the ruled card and the shot is held for the rest of the second. Upper third is plain wall, lower third plain dark desk front.

Frames 960 to 984. The card with its tag holds, the caption clears at 32.4 s. Cut at 32.6 s to a tighter side view, then a large wooden rubber stamp drops in from the top onto the card's left side at 32.8 s, covering the header. No hand holds the stamp.

Frames 990 to 1014. The stamp presses and lifts away leaving a crooked red OWNER COUNT mark on the card beneath the tag. Cut at 33.6 s to a medium back office view: a window, a cork board with an empty black bulldog clip, the card small on the desk with the tag and stamp. Clip has not moved yet.

Frames 1020 to 1044. Medium office shot held; the bulldog clip on the cork board opens a little and snaps shut on nothing, wobbling. The clip is small, about a tenth of frame width. Card with tag and OWNER COUNT mark sits small on the desk. Bottom half is plain dark desk front.

Frames 1050 to 1074. Kitchen pass with an empty-ish glass jar on the shelf and a wok on the range at right; a paid phone is held up at left on a long arm. From 35.6 s coins pop out of the phone screen and arc toward the jar. Caption names FOX 26.

Frames 1080 to 1104. A stream of coins and green notes arcs from the paid phone into the jar on the pass. Cut at 36.6 s to a close jar; coins fall in through the mouth and the pile inside grows. Coins are drawn in perspective with highlights.

Frames 1110 to 1134. The last coins and notes fall into the jar and the pile rises to about two thirds. At 37.8 s a larger detail of the full jar, whose middle is covered by the caption band. No tag yet.

Frames 1140 to 1164. A kraft tag reading FOX 26 reports / all to the kitchen is carried in from the right on a string and hooks at the jar's neck, hanging over the upper jar by 38.8 s. The caption band crosses the jar's lower half and coin pile.

Frames 1170 to 1194. The FOX 26 tag hangs and settles on the full jar; caption clears. At 39.6 s cut to an almost empty wooden desk front view with only the edge of a white card at the right edge; most of the frame is plain desk and dark desk front.

Frames 1200 to 1224. A cream rule card titled Federal tip pool rule slides in from the right and settles on the desk; its text reads If the employer takes no tip credit / a tip pool may include cooks, with a small chef hat icon. At 40.8 s a checkbox outline is being drawn beside the no tip credit line. Card fills about two thirds of frame width.

Frames 1230 to 1254. The rule card rests on the desk with its empty checkbox completed beside no tip credit. No sampled change through this second; the shot holds while the caption reads When the employer takes no tip credit.

Frames 1260 to 1284. The settled rule card holds unchanged through 42.6 s (about 1.4 s static since settling plus this page). At 42.8 s a closer framing of the card; a thin butter highlight starts at the left of the cooks line. Caption switches to federal rules allow a tip pool with cooks.

Frames 1290 to 1314. Close on the rule card: a butter highlight wipes across a tip pool may include cooks from left to right, reaching the chef hat by 43.8 s. The no tip credit box stays empty. Text legible at this size.

Frames 1320 to 1344. A writing hand with a pen reaches up from the bottom and begins circling the card's lines; at 44.4 to 44.6 s the hand covers the no tip credit text. By 44.8 s the hand has left frame while a partial ink loop runs over the box and down the right edge. Box remains unticked.

Frames 1350 to 1374. The ink loop closes around the no tip credit line, the box and the highlighted cooks line. The writing hand then stays parked over the upper left of the card through 45.8 s, its fist and sleeve covering much of the header and the no tip credit and cooks words. Box still unticked.

Frames 1380 to 1404. Cut to a wide desk with the circled rule card cropped at the left edge and a large empty desk area. From 46.6 s a closed manila folder tabbed Restaurant slides in from the right. The rule card and folder are small, upper half only.

Frames 1410 to 1434. The Restaurant folder settles beside the rule card, then a cut to a close view as its cover opens to reveal a page headed Takes no tip credit? with a single empty checkbox. No question mark yet.
Frames 1440 to 1464. The open folder page reading Takes no tip credit? holds with its box empty, then a large question mark fades and scales in beside the box, solid by 48.8 s. Legible at phone size.

Frames 1470 to 1494. The folder question mark holds, then a cut to the table with the code card; a hand raises a phone with a dimmed, blurred camera view toward the code. Same skin tone and sleeve as the earlier scanning guest. Caption at 49.8 s quotes one customer about QR codes.

Frames 1500 to 1524. The hand holds the phone up beside the code card, its camera view not closing on the code, then lowers it toward the bottom by 50.8 s with the screen dimming. The phone partly overlaps the code card at peak. Caption quotes the customer remark.

Frames 1530 to 1554. The phone is lowered, then a cut to a wider table where the phone lies flat and small near the code stand. A quote card reading "not very convenient for every kind of people" / One customer slides in from the right and settles beside the stand, its right edge cut by the frame. Objects are small in a mostly empty pale frame.

Frames 1560 to 1584. The quote card has landed to the right of the code stand, beside the lowered phone, and the shot holds still. The three objects form a thin band across mid-frame; the rest of the frame is empty wall and table. Quote text is small but readable.

Frames 1590 to 1614. The quote card scene holds while the lowered phone's screen darkens. At 53.8 s a cut to a medium view of the room: the lit Haniya panel on its pole, and at the right a steel pass with the full tip jar and the printer with its ticket. Jar and printer are small at the right edge.

Frames 1620 to 1644. In the medium room shot the panel shows an order card rising, then a small ticket slip leaves the panel and arcs on a dashed line toward the printer on the pass at right. Order card and slip are small, roughly a twentieth of frame width. No guest is shown at the panel.

Frames 1650 to 1674. The small slip completes its arc and disappears into the printer at the right edge by 55.4 s; the room then holds still with the panel showing the order card. No sampled change from 55.4 s to 55.8 s.

Frames 1680 to 1704. The medium room holds static for about 1.2 s more (since 55.4 s), then a cut at 56.8 s to a close full tip jar on the shelf as a cream tag starting with ow slides in from the right. Caption: and who gets the tip rests on the owner's word.

Frames 1710 to 1734. A cream tag reading owner says is carried in from the right and hooks onto the full jar's neck, hanging over its upper coins by 57.8 s. Jar about a sixth of frame height, upper middle. Caption band below the jar.

Frames 1740 to 1764. The owner says tag hangs on the close jar, then a cut at 58.4 s to a wide shot with the panel at left and the jar on the pass at right. A second tag reading no record shown enters from the left and passes in front of the panel's pole and lower screen on its way toward the jar.

Frames 1770 to 1794. The no record shown tag swings across from the left and settles hanging under the owner says tag on the jar's neck. Together the two tags cover most of the jar so the coins are barely visible. Panel remains lit at left.

Frames 1800 to 1824. The closing wide image with the panel and the two-tagged jar holds for about a second, caption clears at 60.2 s, then at 60.6 s the dark credits card appears with the Lone Star flag, the Texas AI Docket wordmark, the URL and the source list.
Frames 1830 to 1854. The dark credits card holds unchanged: Lone Star flag, Texas AI Docket, texasaidocket.com, four sources and the illustration credit.
Frames 1860 to 1884. Credits card unchanged across all five samples: flag, Texas AI Docket, texasaidocket.com, sources and illustration credit.
Frames 1890 to 1914. Credits card unchanged: Lone Star flag, Texas AI Docket wordmark, texasaidocket.com, four sources, illustration credit.
Frames 1920 to 1944. The credits card is unchanged across all five samples, with flag, wordmark, URL, sources and illustration credit.
Frames 1950 to 1963, the last page of option A. The credits card stays unchanged to the final frame at 65.433 s.

Frames 0 to 24. Overhead plan of a small restaurant occupying the upper half of the frame: two round tables with guests seen from above, a host stand by a door on the left wall, a steel counter at right. A trail of footprints appears from the stand out the door while the door leaf swings shut along a dashed arc. Lower half is plain cream.

Frames 30 to 54. The overhead plan holds: the door leaf is closed, a trail of dark footprints runs from the host stand out through the doorway, and small ring marks pulse near the hinge. Plan fills the upper half; caption sits just below it.

Frames 60 to 84. The plan holds with the footprint trail while the Texas locator card draws in. Cut at 2.6 s to a medium view of the host stand with its desk phone and a dark apron hanging from the side hook; the caption band overlaps the stand body and the apron's lower half.

Frames 90 to 114. Medium host stand shot held; the desk phone rings in pulses with arc marks and nobody answers. The caption band covers the lower stand and the apron's lower half. Locator card completes.

Frames 120 to 144. The medium host stand holds; the phone keeps ringing in pulses. When the caption clears at 4.6 s the full apron hanging from the stand hook and the stand base are visible. No one appears.

Frames 150 to 174. Close view over the host stand: a blank ruled pad with a pencil lies on top while behind, a guest in orange holding a menu raises a hand and a second guest sits at right. The pad's corner curls and stays blank. Large plain wash fills the upper half. Caption crosses the stand front.

Frames 180 to 204. Same close shot over the host stand: the orange guest holds a hand up toward the empty stand while the phone at left rings. The pad stays blank. Upper half of frame is an empty pale wash.

Frames 210 to 234. The close stand shot holds with the raised hand until 7.6 s. At 7.8 s cut to a wide storefront: door, empty sign frame on the glass, a dark flat panel on a pole, one small guest at a table and the host stand at right with its apron. All objects sit in the middle band of the frame.

Frames 240 to 264. Wide storefront view: the blank sign frame on the glass swings slightly and settles with nothing pinned in it while the panel beside it stays dark. Objects occupy the middle band; the lower third is floor.
Frames 270 to 294. The wide storefront holds unchanged: blank sign frame upright, dark panel, seated guest and host stand. No sampled motion during this second.

Frames 300 to 324. Wide storefront unchanged; the panel remains dark and the sign frame still. Caption clears at 10.6 s. With the previous page, the picture has been static from about 8.8 s to 10.8 s.

Frames 330 to 354. Medium view of the panel on its pole standing beside the host stand where the apron still hangs. The screen lights from the left and the name Haniya writes across it by 11.8 s. The caption sits over the pole and stand base.
Frames 360 to 384. The lit Haniya panel beside the empty host stand is held without visible change. No tag yet.

Frames 390 to 414. Cut at 13.4 s to a large detail of the lit panel reading Haniya. A slate tag reading AI host is carried in on a string from the upper left and reaches the panel's top left corner by 13.8 s. Caption crosses the panel's lower screen.
Frames 420 to 444. The AI host tag swings across and hooks at the panel's corner eyelet, then settles over the upper right of the lit screen next to the rings. Haniya stays centered and legible.

Frames 450 to 474. The tagged panel holds to 15.4 s, then a cut to an overhead table: a code card in its stand sits at center with a plate, menu, chopsticks and glass. A hand-held phone at lower left already displays a camera view of a code. No caption at 15.6 to 15.8 s.

Frames 480 to 504. From above, a hand with a blue sleeve raises the phone from the bottom edge up across the table toward the code card; its screen shows the code. It passes through the caption band at 16.2 to 16.4 s and stops just short of, and partly over, the code stand at 16.8 s.

Frames 510 to 534. Overhead: the phone is held over the code stand, which it mostly hides; its screen shows the code locked in brackets. A long forearm and blue sleeve run from the bottom edge. At 17.8 s the menu sheet begins rising on screen.

Frames 540 to 564. From above, the menu slides up on the held phone and replaces the camera view; the open menu shows dish rows and a Pay button, all very small at this scale. The phone hides the code stand beneath.

Frames 570 to 594. Cut at 19.2 s to a medium view: a seated guest sits small at left behind a table, while a phone held by a large hand in the foreground shows the menu. A second hand on a long blue-sleeved arm from the right edge taps the Chow mein row, which lights yellow at 19.8 s. The holding arm rises from the bottom edge and neither arm visibly connects to the seated guest.

Frames 600 to 624. The tapping finger lifts off and withdraws down to the right, crossing in front of the code card at 20.2 s, and leaves frame by 20.4 s. The Chow mein row stays lit on the held phone. No Talk use shown.

Frames 630 to 654. The medium shot holds briefly without caption, then a cut to a large detail of the phone's lower screen: Chow mein lit at top, Talk and a big Pay button. No holding hand is visible in the detail. A fingertip enters from the lower right at 21.8 s. The disclosure chip overlaps the phone's upper left.

Frames 660 to 684. A large finger presses Pay; the button turns into a red check reading Paid and a big white Paid card with a red check rises over the menu. The finger leaves and the Paid state is held, large and legible.

Frames 690 to 714. The large Paid confirmation is held, then a cut at 23.6 s to a wide kitchen with a hood, a small printer on a steel cabinet under a rail and heat lamp, and an empty wok on an unlit range. Printer and wok each occupy a small part of the frame.

Frames 720 to 744. The idle wide kitchen holds, then a cut at 24.6 s to the overhead room plan with a tiny paid phone on the lower table. At 24.8 s a red dashed line runs from that phone toward the printer on the right counter while the view starts pushing in.

Frames 750 to 774. The camera pushes in from the plan following the red paid mark along its dashed line, past the jar top, into the printer's slot seen from above at 25.4 s; at 25.6 s the printer's lamp shows red. At 25.8 s a cut to a side view of the printer under its rail with the red lamp lit and an empty slot; the caption crosses the printer's lower half.

Frames 780 to 804. A Chow mein ticket with a red check rises from the printer slot, reaches the rail and hangs by 26.4 s. Cut to a closer kitchen detail: the ticket hangs above the printer while a cook's sleeved arm brings a steel bowl from the right and pours noodles into the wok as orange flames flare. Only the arm is visible.

Frames 810 to 834. The bowl finishes and leaves; the wok, full of noodles, sits in tall orange flames while the cook's hand at the right edge rocks the handle and the noodles toss. The printed ticket hangs above the red-lamped printer throughout. Wok and printer fill the upper middle.

Frames 840 to 864. Overhead view of an empty wooden desk with a mug and a black receipt clip. From 28.4 s a ruled ledger card headed Saving or winning back slides in from the right edge. The desk fills the upper half; lower half is plain cream.

Frames 870 to 894. From above, the ruled ledger card slides to the middle of the desk and settles, header Saving or winning back clearly legible, rows empty. The figure is only in the caption at this point.

Frames 900 to 924. Closer overhead view of the ledger card. A large kraft tag reading $9,650 a month falls in from the upper right, scaling down as it nears the card, and lands flat on the card's right side at 30.8 s. Legible and large.

Frames 930 to 954. The $9,650 a month tag lies flat on the ledger card, held still for the rest of the second. Header and tag both large and legible; lower half of frame is plain cream below the desk.

Frames 960 to 984. The card with its tag is held, caption clears at 32.4 s. From 32.6 s a large rubber stamp seen from above swoops in from the upper right, shrinking toward the card as it nears, and by 32.8 s hovers over the card below the tag with a shadow. No hand holds the stamp.

Frames 990 to 1014. The stamp presses on the card and lifts away at 33.4 s, revealing a crooked red OWNER COUNT mark below the header (the tag is briefly hidden under the stamp). Cut at 33.6 s to a medium office: window, cork board with an empty bulldog clip, mug, and the small stamped card on the desk. Lower third is dark desk front.
Frames 1020 to 1044. Medium office held; the bulldog clip on the cork board opens a little and snaps shut on nothing. The clip and card are small; about half the frame is plain dark desk front.

Frames 1050 to 1074. Overhead of the kitchen pass: a paid phone lies at lower left, a jar top with a few coins sits mid-right, wok and printer tops beyond. From 35.2 s coins and a green note emerge from the phone and move across the steel toward the jar. Objects are small in the upper half; lower half plain cream.

Frames 1080 to 1104. From above, a chain of coins and notes slides from the phone to the jar top. Cut at 36.6 s to a side view of the pass: the printer with its hanging ticket, the glass jar, and the wok over flame; coins and a note fall from above into the jar's mouth onto a small pile. The ticket printer in the same shot links back to the paid order.

Frames 1110 to 1134. In the medium pass shot the jar fills to about two thirds as the last coins and notes fall in, beside the printer with its ticket. At 37.8 s a close view of the full jar with the caption band across its middle.

Frames 1140 to 1164. A kraft tag reading FOX 26 reports / all to the kitchen is carried in from the left and hooks at the full jar's neck, settling over its upper half by 38.8 s. The caption band crosses the coin pile below the tag.

Frames 1170 to 1194. The FOX 26 tag settles on the full jar, caption clears and the whole jar is visible at 39.4 s. Cut at 39.6 s to an overhead empty desk with a mug; only the edge of a white card shows at the right edge.

Frames 1200 to 1224. From above, the federal rule card slides in from the right and settles on the desk; at 40.8 s the empty checkbox beside no tip credit is drawing. Card is legible but occupies only about a third of the frame height.
Frames 1230 to 1254. The rule card rests centered on the desk with its empty checkbox, held without change through this second.

Frames 1260 to 1284. The settled rule card on the desk holds unchanged until 42.6 s (static from about 40.8 s, roughly 1.8 s). At 42.8 s a closer view of the card with larger text and a highlight just starting on the cooks line.

Frames 1290 to 1314. Close overhead of the rule card, its left edge just off frame: a butter highlight wipes across a tip pool may include cooks to the chef hat by 43.8 s. The no tip credit box remains empty.

Frames 1320 to 1344. A writing hand on a long purple-sleeved arm reaches up from the bottom left and starts circling the card; at 44.6 s it covers the left half of the card text, at 44.8 s it has moved right and the ink loop runs over the top and round the box. The box stays unticked.

Frames 1350 to 1374. The ink ellipse closes around the no tip credit line, the box and the highlighted cooks line. The pen and hand withdraw to the upper left edge, slightly covering the first letters of the header. Box remains empty. Text stays readable.

Frames 1380 to 1404. Wide overhead of the desk: the circled rule card sits small at upper left and most of the desk is empty. At 46.8 s a closed manila folder tabbed Restaurant slides in from the right edge.

Frames 1410 to 1434. From above, the Restaurant folder slides beside the circled rule card, then a cut to a close overhead of the folder as its cover opens to reveal Takes no tip credit? with an empty box. Large and legible.
Frames 1440 to 1464. The open folder page with its empty box holds, then a question mark fades and scales in beside the box, solid by 48.8 s. Legible.

Frames 1470 to 1494. The folder with its question mark holds, then a cut to the same overhead table as the earlier scan; a hand raises a phone from the lower right with its camera showing the code. The caption at 49.8 s crosses the phone screen.

Frames 1500 to 1524. From above, the hand raises the phone short of the code stand, wavers, then sets it down on the table below the stand with the screen dimming; at 50.8 s the hand withdraws downward, leaving the phone. A pale, stretched hand fragment appears between the table edge and caption at 50.8 s.

Frames 1530 to 1554. The dimmed phone lies on the table below the code stand. From 51.4 s a quote card drops in from the upper left, shrinking as it falls, and by 51.8 s lies over the plate and partly over the code stand. Quote text readable.

Frames 1560 to 1584. From above, the quote card has landed beside the code stand with the dimmed phone lying below, and the shot holds still. Quote text is small but legible at phone size; the table fills the upper half.

Frames 1590 to 1614. The table holds as the lowered phone's screen goes dark. At 53.8 s a cut to a wide room: the lit Haniya panel at left, a small seated guest by the window, and the steel pass at right with the printer, its hanging ticket and the full tip jar. Elements are small within the frame.

Frames 1620 to 1644. In the wide room an order card rises on the Haniya panel and a small ticket slip leaves the panel along a dashed arc toward the printer on the pass. The seated guest does not interact with the panel. All elements are small, the panel about a sixth of frame height.
Frames 1650 to 1674. The slip finishes its arc into the printer at 55.2 s and disappears; the wide room then holds unchanged from 55.4 to 55.8 s with the order card on the panel.

Frames 1680 to 1704. The wide room with the panel and pass holds static from 55.4 s to 56.6 s (about 1.2 s). At 56.8 s a cut to a medium view of the pass: printer with its ticket beside the full tip jar, and a cream tag starting with ow entering from the right.

Frames 1710 to 1734. A cream tag reading owner says is carried in from the right and hooks on the full jar's neck beside the printer and its ticket, settling over the upper coins by 57.8 s. Both jar and printer are mid-size in the upper middle.

Frames 1740 to 1764. The owner says tag hangs on the jar in the medium pass, then a cut at 58.4 s to a closer detail with the printer and its Chow mein ticket above and the tagged jar below. A second tag ending in rd shown slides in from the left toward the jar.

Frames 1770 to 1794. The no record shown tag swings in and settles hanging below the owner says tag on the jar's neck; the printer with its Chow mein ticket stays above. Both tags are large and legible; the coin pile is mostly hidden behind the tags and the caption band.

Frames 1800 to 1824. The closing detail of the printer with its Chow mein ticket above the full jar wearing owner says and no record shown tags holds; the caption clears at 60.2 s and the full jar is visible. At 60.6 s the dark credits card appears.
Frames 1830 to 1854 of option B. Static dark credits card with the flag, Texas AI Docket wordmark, URL, four sources and illustration credit. This page's image hash equals option A's page 061.
